quest.title: Where Flowers Awaken
quest.description: Following a tranquil stay in Nod-Krai, you check in with Katheryne to see if anything noteworthy has happened lately.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1000, Mora x44000, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

chapter.num: Song of the Welkin Moon: Act IX
chapter.title: As All Falls to Emptiness

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: #Ah, {NICKNAME}, Paimon. It's been a while.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: As it happens, there is a letter here for you. One moment... Here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A letter? From who?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: (Dear diary, I'm Collei. I work as a trainee Forest Ranger under my master, Tighnari. I'm also studying at the Akademiya.)

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: (I've been getting better and better at reading lately. Mr. Alhaitham says that the written word is a crucial medium for exploring the world and understanding oneself. That's why I decided to start this diary...)

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: (That said, what should I write about? Things are pretty quiet in Sumeru these days. Life is good. Every day is a fulfilling and happy one.)

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: (When I think back to the days when I suffered from Eleazar, or way back to when I was injected with god remains... I'm in a much better place now. I hope it stays that way forever.)

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: (I'll leave it there for now. Master said he'll take me shopping in Sumeru City today, which is great, because I've been meaning to visit the toy seller at the Grand Bazaar for a while now...)

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Collei, time to go!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Yes, Master... Huh!?

talks.objective: Discuss the current situation with Sethos

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: What's wrong, Collei? Is there something on my face...?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: N—No, sorry — I didn't mean to stare. Did Master Tighnari send you to pick me up?

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: "Master Tighnari"? Haha, what are you talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Tighnari is the General Mahamatra. He's probably busy arresting criminals in Sumeru City... Heh, I mean, if that's what floats your boat, I can introduce you, but...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Wait, Master Tighnari is the General Mahamatra? But what about Mr. Cyno?

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Sorry?

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Oh oh oh, you mean that guy who just joined the Vahumana Darshan? Rumor has it he's the leader of the Temple of Silence. If that's true, it's pretty impressive.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Sounds like you've been getting to know more and more people since you joined the Akademiya. That's great, but don't let your Forest Ranger duties fall by the wayside, okay?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: (What's going on? Sethos is acting like he's my master, and Master Tighnari has taken over Mr. Cyno's job. Is this some kind of prank?)

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: (If so, it's a weird choice of prank... But anyway, Sethos doesn't look like he's joking. What is this all about?)

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Hey, you're zoning out again. I'm gonna buy some tools for the rangers. Why don't you stretch your legs a bit? It's been a while since you last visited the city, right?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Wait...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: (He's right... It has been a while since I last visited Sumeru City. Was it always like this? I mean, it feels familiar, yet somehow... Something seems different...)

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: (Is this really Sumeru City...?)

dialogues.speaker: Qasimi
dialogues.text: Lord Kaveh Bay, did you get a chance to review this month's accounts? Any feedback?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Yawn... You mean, the version you sent over a few days ago? Yeah, I took a look when I received it.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I was thinking that maybe our profit margin is a little excessive? I visited some of our commercial partners last month. Their earnings are very slim.

dialogues.speaker: Qasimi
dialogues.text: Are you suggesting that we give up some of our profits for them?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Well, since we have more than we need, yes. Making money for its own sake is pointless. Don't worry, I've already planned for it, and the numbers look fine. We can adjust the rates starting from next month.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Also, about that designer you hired... I've had to revise his proposal three times now, but he just doesn't seem to.... *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Let's cut our losses. Pay him his fee and send him on his way. I'd like you to get Layla on this instead. She was Cyrus's student and she designed the Palace of Alcazarzaray. Seems like a much safer choice...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Hmm? Who's sneaking around over there?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: ...Mr. Kaveh?

dialogues.speaker: Hisham
dialogues.text: Do you recognize this person, Sir?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Yes, it's alright, We've met. This is Collei, Sethos's trainee. He brought her along the last time I went for drinks with him.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: What brings you to the city, Collei? Is your master here too?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: (No, no, this is all wrong! Why is Mr. Kaveh saying that too? Tighnari's my master, not Sethos!)

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: (This can't be real... I have to ask someone else. There's gotta be someone else out there who still remembers the truth!)

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...Hey, wait, don't run off! How strange... What's gotten into her today?

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Lots of visitors today, I see! Welcome, all, it's been a while.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hey, Rahman. You know that guy who sells face powder on Treasures Street? I haven't seen him around in a while. Any idea what happened to him?

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Oh, you mean Ahangar? Yeah, he got into a brawl with Shevirme on Treasures Street... He's been banned from setting up shop there for now.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Seriously? Well, that's a shame. I was planning to pick out some makeup for you...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Oh, don't worry about it.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: The legendary "Flame-Mane" discussing makeup with the Zubayr Theater's star dancer... Haha. Now there's something you don't see every day.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Flame-Mane...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: You know, I'm not actually sure when people started calling me that. Maybe the other Eremites thought I needed a fiercer title to scare people off?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: To be completely honest, I think the title would fit you better than me, Dehya.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: You think? Haha, can't say I've never imagined myself as a merc. If I ever give up the dancing, maybe I'll head to the desert and give the Eremite life a try.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: You would?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Is that so strange?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Oh, not at all. In fact, I've actually had similar thoughts before... If I ever get tired of sleeping out in the wild, I think I might go look for a job at the Zubayr Theater.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: I've adored the Dance of Sabzeruz ever since the first time I saw you perform it. If the chance ever came up, I'd love to try it out on stage for myself.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Really? If our manager, Setaria heard you say that, she'd hold you to it. Probably grab you by the sleeve and never let you go again.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hey, when that day comes, I'll do your makeup myself. How's that sound?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Sure! If the day comes, I'd be honored.

dialogues.speaker: Ilyas
dialogues.text: Mahamatra Tighnari, we've apprehended the suspect.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: They say that the fool is prone to blind faith, but the wise man is not immune to it either.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Siraj, do you have anything to say in your defense?

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: Tighnari...! You were the one who turned the sages against me! Just a few words of caution from you was all it took to destroy my research!

dialogues.speaker: Siraj
dialogues.text: And now you're trying to stop me again? You should know that mechanical life is the future. We must cast aside our useless flesh and—

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: That's enough. I'm not in the mood to listen to your lunacy. Anyone could tell you how amateur your work is.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Kareena, Ilyas, put him somewhere safely out of the way.

dialogues.speaker: Kareena
dialogues.text: ...Yes, sir!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Next on the agenda is... Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: ...Master?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: What is it? ...Wait, did Professor Zaha Hadi send you? She's been encouraging me to take on an apprentice... Might be getting a bit ahead of herself there, though.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: No! Master, it's me! Collei!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Listen to me, something really weird is going on in Sumeru City. It's like everyone's identities have switched around...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: You're not the General Mahamatra, you're a Forest Watcher! Just yesterday, we agreed to come to Sumeru City today to go shopping together, and—

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Alright, there's no rush. Let's back up a little.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Your name is Collei, correct? Although this is our first meeting, you do seem strangely familiar somehow. Is there anything I can help you with?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: No, no...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Master, Master...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Did you have another nightmare?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I've told you before, when you're tired, lay down on your back in bed and get some proper sleep. It's much better for you than napping on your front. Poor posture obstructs your breathing, which can lead to all sorts of weird dreams.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Now, we're supposed to go shopping in Sumeru City today, remember? Cheer up, I'll take you to Hushang's. I heard he's got some new toys in stock.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Go wash your face, take some deep breaths, and when you're ready, we'll head out.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: O—Okay! Thanks, Master Tighnari.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: (Huh... So it was just a dream.)
And yet, dreams can sometimes be a warning of things that will soon come to pass.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Wh—Who who said that!?
That dream felt unusually real, didn't it? Here's my suggestion... Since you're heading into Sumeru City anyway, you may as well tell Lesser Lord Kusanali about everything that happened.
And just to be on the safe side, I think you should also inform your two traveler friends who once helped save Sumeru. I'd write them a letter if I were you.
Time is short... A storm is coming from beyond the bounds of fate.

talks.objective: Discuss the letter's contents with Paimon

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What a strange situation... No wonder Collei was in such a rush to write us a letter.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Imagine waking up one day to find that everything around you has changed. You might not even recognize Paimon anymore... Ohh, that's a scary thought!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's get to Sumeru and find out what the heck is going on!

talks.objective: Enter Sumeru City to check on the situation

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Collei!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon! Thank goodness. I'm so glad you made it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course! We won't let anything happen to you, Collei. So, what's going on in Sumeru City? Looks like lots of people are moving, or something?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Yeah, I was just gonna say.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: After I wrote my letter, Master and I went to Sumeru City and told the Dendro Archon everything that I experienced, from start to finish.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What did Nahida say?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: She was silent at first. It seemed like she was deep in thought... Then, the next day, we got told that she was ordering everyone to leave Sumeru City immediately and move to Caravan Ribat.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...The entire population of the city has to move?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Not just Sumeru City. The evacuation also includes Lokapala Jungle, Avidya Forest, Ashavan Realm, and Ardravi Valley...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Basically, everyone living in the rainforest must temporarily relocate to Caravan Ribat.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Holy smokes... That's crazy!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Yes, it's quite an operation. Even if people only bring the bare essentials, the scale is simply enormous.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: They've requisitioned almost all the Sumpter Beasts in Sumeru for the task. Including the entirety of Dori's Sumpter Beast Park.

choices.text: All on account of that dream Collei had?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: The Dendro Archon said that what Collei experienced was not a dream, but a warning.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: After our meeting, she immediately summoned the six sages to analyze the situation and discuss countermeasures. They concluded that the events seen in the dream are very likely to become a reality, and that an unknown danger is rapidly approaching.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Oh, uh, please keep that to yourself. We don't want to cause widespread panic.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: The official reason they've given is a large-scale renovation of the rainforest's ecosystem. People are skeptical, but there haven't been any major incidents. So far, at least.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: The Dendro Archon seemed really worried when we spoke to her... She said you can go visit her in the Sanctuary of Surasthana when you arrive.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: She also said she'd hold out until the very end.

response.speaker: Amir
response.text: Tighnari, Collei, you got a minute? I need a hand here...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: One moment, I'll be right there!

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: As a Forest Watcher, I've been tasked with assisting with the relocation work. There's a lot to be done, and they need all the help they can get.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: This will be the final group of evacuees from Sumeru City. While they're away from home, they'll be heavily reliant on outside help.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Thank you for coming in our time of need. As you can see, another crisis is upon us.

response.speaker: Aryadeva
response.text: Excuse me... Sorry to trouble you, but could you help an old man find his medicine? It's buried somewhere in my luggage.

response.speaker: Amid
response.text: Where's my mom? Where did she go? *sob*...

response.speaker: Amir
response.text: Phew... Don't worry, it'll be okay...

response.speaker: Hatim
response.text: Those items are worth a small fortune. Make sure you store them somewhere safe, you understand?

response.speaker: Rima
response.text: I bet you thought you'd get away with this in the chaos, huh? Guess again! No petty thief gets past me.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (A mass evacuation inevitably comes with all kinds of problems. Nahida wouldn't have resorted to this unless it was absolutely necessary.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (The strange events of Collei's dream took place in Sumeru City... Whatever danger is afoot, it must start here, which is why everyone has to leave.)

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: We should go help the evacuees. See you around.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Um... I'm so glad that you believed me and came all this way to help. It means a lot. Please stay safe.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't worry! We may not know exactly what's going on yet, but as long as we stick together, we'll find a way through this!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Goodbye! Look after yourselves!

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Will do, see ya!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Phew... Paimon's not sure how she found the words to comfort Collei, because honestly, she's kinda nervous herself...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's head to the Sanctuary of Surasthana and see Nahida.

choices.text: Did Nahida give any indication as to why?

talks.objective: Go to the Sanctuary of Surasthana

dialogues.speaker: Mu'tasim
dialogues.text: Who goes there!? No unauthorized access to this place, by order of Mahamatra Cyno!

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: Ahem...

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: #Are you blind? It's {NICKNAME} and Paimon... Surely, you've seen them before?

dialogues.speaker: Mu'tasim
dialogues.text: Huh? Oh... So it is. I'm sorry, I haven't been sleeping well lately. My nerves are a little frayed.

response.speaker: Mu'tasim
response.text: ...The Dendro Archon is in a very vulnerable state at the moment. Mahamatra Cyno is concerned that our enemies might choose this moment to strike, so he's ordered us to strengthen our defenses.

response.speaker: Aarav
response.text: Just seeing you two again already puts our minds at ease. Please, enter. I'm sure everyone's expecting you.

talks.objective: Learn about the situation from everyone

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon. You made it.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Aha! Perfect timing! Reliable helpers like you are just what we need right now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's good to see everyone again. Collei gave us a rough idea of what's going on, but we still have a lot of questions.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What kind of danger is Sumeru City in, exactly? And how come everyone has to move to Caravan Ribat?

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: At this stage, we can't be certain. We're investigating, but no definitive answers yet.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I take it that Collei told you about her strange dream?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah. Apparently, everyone in Sumeru City was acting super weird. Even you guys. It was like you'd all switched places.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: That's right. Collei and Tighnari reported the situation to the Dendro Archon. She believes that it wasn't merely a dream — and that whatever it was has something to do with Irminsul.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: It's a reasonable inference. Only through Irminsul can people's memory and cognition be so significantly modified in such a short time.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: We don't know why Collei would dream of these things, nor who was trying to warn her. The Dendro Archon decided to connect to Irminsul to investigate more thoroughly.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Has she found anything yet?

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Irminsul is connected directly to the Ley Lines. The tree serves as a central hub where the Ley Lines converge, and its core function is to record and store the world's knowledge and memories.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: But something has gone awry, severely compromising the performance of this core function.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Information is bottlenecking inside Irminsul, hampering the Ley Lines' flow. If this continues, new information will languish unrecorded, with existing records thrown into disarray.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: In short, the souls of the dead will be stranded, while the living have their sense of reality warped.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: In the long run, Collei's dream could well become a reality. And that's just the beginning. There's no telling what other nightmares could end up coming true.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Irminsul... the Ley Lines...)

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: I have come this far to use my death to open the gates of the Ley Lines to my people.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (In Natlan, The Captain was storing stranded souls inside his own heart. It was only after the rules of the Night Kingdom were amended that they were finally able to return to the Ley Lines...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (And that was just one nation. A problem with Irminsul itself could end up affecting all Ley Lines worldwide...)

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Faced with a growing backlog of information, the Dendro Archon decided to connect herself directly to Irminsul and take over the recording and processing function herself.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: But it's an almost impossible task. Individual brains aren't equipped to deal with the sheer volume of knowledge and memories involved. All that information flooding in at once would instantly fry any human mind.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: And for a god... *sigh*. Even for a god, the suffering must be unimaginable.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: The Dendro Archon's power originates from Irminsul. Any issue with the tree itself takes a toll on her to begin with.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: On top of that, she's subjecting herself to the grueling task of processing all that data... It must be torture for her.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: And despite all of this, she is somehow finding the strength to investigate the Irminsul situation from within, and send us her findings...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I've finished analyzing the latest data. Looks like our working theory was wrong. There's no signs of Irminsul having been attacked from the outside.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: So it's internal, then? Some sort of disease, perhaps...? Hmm, no... I've spent half my life studying the Ley Lines. If Irminsul malfunctioned this easily, the world would've met its end long ago.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cyno? What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Not long ago, I got a tip from the Corps of Thirty that a large number of unidentified merchant caravans had recently been spotted entering Sumeru through Bayda Harbor.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: At first, I suspected that they might have something to do with all this, so I sent some people to investigate. But if Irminsul wasn't attacked from the outside...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Don't you think there are more important things to worry about right now than guessing who's behind all this?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: It's been over twelve hours with no new intel. If even the keeper of Irminsul is this badly affected, you can imagine how bad things are in there.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Dendro Archon...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nahida!

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Her breathing is weak! And her elemental energy levels are dangerously low...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Looks like it's time to move to the backup plan.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's the backup plan?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Get out of the city, and take the Dendro Archon with us.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: The entrance to Irminsul is directly beneath the Sanctuary of Surasthana. That means this is ground zero if anything goes wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: The Dendro Archon has a very strong connection to Irminsul, but theoretically, this connection should grow weaker with distance.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Under normal circumstances, she could unleash her full power here. But with Irminsul out of control, our first priority is to get her away from here.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: The situation is critical. There's no time to deliberate. Everyone in agreement?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I'll deal with it. I'll also let the matra and the Corps of Thirty know to start evacuating.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Let's go. No sense grieving when there's nothing more we can do.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Agreed... We'll be back as soon as this is over.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: The last group of civilians has been safely evacuated. The Dendro Archon's carriage will travel with them. Cyno and Hat Guy will protect the convoy.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's good news... But you don't look very relieved.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: With the Dendro Archon in a coma, we've lost our means of investigating the situation.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: And with Irminsul still deteriorating, we have no choice but to evacuate Sumeru City. It feels as though we're being pushed along by an invisible hand...

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Stop moaning, Cyrus. We're the teachers here. We should be showing a little more confidence, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: A wise judgment.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Let's move out. To Caravan Ribat.

dialogues.speaker: Bortnikov
dialogues.text: Sir, all units are in position.
Good. Everything is going to plan. Interfering with Sumeru City is a necessary step, so do not hesitate. The Irminsul situation will not harm you.
We need to speed things up here too. We don't want to keep our client waiting, do we?

dialogues.speaker: Vereshchagina
dialogues.text: No, Sir. You have my word, everything will be completed on schedule.
They say that fervent ambition attracts the favor of the gods — and with it, a Vision.
But we appear to be the exception. So, is our ambition not strong enough... or does it threaten the very foundations of this world?

dialogues.speaker: Akram
dialogues.text: Hey, did you see who just walked by? I think she's that famous merc...

dialogues.speaker: Farooq
dialogues.text: Yeah, it's gotta be her. That red hair gives her away — the "Flame-Mane"... They say she can take down a dozen tough guys with just one hand!

dialogues.speaker: Nizam
dialogues.text: Would you like some fruit?

dialogues.speaker: Tanamart
dialogues.text: How will I ever save enough money to buy that custom-made axe with floral carvings from the blacksmith?

choices.text: What do you need that for?

response.speaker: Tanamart
response.text: To use as a weapon, of course.

response.speaker: Tanamart
response.text: As Housein's secretary, I must ensure his safety. Don't underestimate me just because I'm a homemaker. I used to be a mercenary in the Corps of Thirty.

response.speaker: Tanamart
response.text: Peace is precious, but you must always be prepared for the worst.

response.speaker: Tanamart
response.text: See you. Whether you're at home or heading out, make sure you stay safe.

dialogues.speaker: Housein
dialogues.text: It takes courage to maintain a peaceful life too.

dialogues.speaker: Housein
dialogues.text: Hello, my name is Housein. I'm responsible for managing administrative affairs in the Grand Bazaar and Treasures Street on behalf of the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Housein
dialogues.text: It's always one thing after another... *sigh* If only everyone was as good-natured as the great merchant Kaveh Bay.

dialogues.speaker: Nawid
dialogues.text: When I grow up, I'm gonna join the Eremites and protect Sumeru City!

dialogues.speaker: Rima
dialogues.text: I heard that the sage disappears without a trace as soon as he gets off work. It's a little mysterious if you ask me...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: *sigh* Remember a while back when I was working on a renovation plan for the House of Daena? Well, I submitted a report to the Grand Sage, and he rejected it!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: It's infuriating! How does someone with no sense of aesthetics whatsoever even become the Grand Sage?

dialogues.speaker: Qasimi
dialogues.text: Please, calm down, Lord Kaveh. Maybe it's for the best that the proposal wasn't approved. Weren't you planning on paying for the renovations out of your own pocket? The Grand Sage just saved you a huge sum of Mora.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...You're right. It's his loss if he doesn't want to work with me. Let him live out the rest of his days in an artless void for all I care! Hmph!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Anyway, enough about that killjoy. There's supposed to be a show at the Zubayr Theater today. Are you guys free later? Tickets are on me if you want to join.

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: The Grand Sage always used to disappear the moment he got off work. But recently, for whatever reason, he's been seen sifting through records in the House of Daena late into the night.

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: We asked him if there was anything unusual going on, but he answered us with a question of his own: "Don't you find it strange that someone with my personality would willingly accept the position of sage?"

dialogues.speaker: Zohreh
dialogues.text: Hey bud, can I ask you a favor? Is it alright if I borrow your thesis?

dialogues.speaker: Zohreh
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I'm not gonna copy your work. I just need it as a reference.

dialogues.speaker: Sanad
dialogues.text: I guess that's okay... but if our theses end up sounding too similar, it's gonna be easy for them to spot.

dialogues.speaker: Zohreh
dialogues.text: Yeah, trust me, plagiarism's the last thing on my mind. The only reason I ask is, it's been really hard to get my hands on any reference material lately...

dialogues.speaker: Sanad
dialogues.text: Why don't you go ask the Grand Conservator? Candace should be able to find you what you need. She's super friendly, I'm sure she'll be happy to help.

dialogues.speaker: Zohreh
dialogues.text: Really? I always assumed she'd be tough to negotiate with... Fair enough. I'll try my luck at the House of Daena later, then.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Would you like a cup of coffee?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: The store's been pretty busy lately. Lots of customers have been feeding Ashru, who watches over the shop, and now Ashru's put on quite a lot of weight... Maybe I should put up a sign saying "Please Don't Feed the Cat"?

dialogues.speaker: Alrani
dialogues.text: Students are under so much pressure these days. Sometimes, I just want to write their papers for them.

dialogues.speaker: Alrani
dialogues.text: Peculiar papers come to me for review every day. I really wish they were able to relax once in a while and not be constantly plagued by academic conundrums. It doesn't do a person any good to spend too long down the rabbit hole.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Nilou, have you been to Aaru Village recently? I've got a friend who I haven't seen in a while... I was wondering how she's doing.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: You mean Faruzan? The guardian of Aaru Village? I saw her not too long ago. She seemed completely absorbed in her research.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: No change there, then... I'll have to catch up with her the next time I'm out that way.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Alright, not a single Mora short. That covers you for this month's rent.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: What a relief... I was worried the design fees I received this month wouldn't be enough.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Well, next time, don't fret — just let me know, and I'll give you a few days' grace. We've known each other long enough for that! Anyway, how are you settling in? I couldn't help but notice that you're staying up late quite often.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Yeah... I can't explain it, I just feel more inspired at night. Once I get in the zone, I can race through a whole bunch of drafts, no problem.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: But what about you? I keep hearing you sighing these days... Is everything okay?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Well, it's just... Don't you think this house is a little small?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: I guess I should be used to it after living here for so many years... But for some reason, I've been feeling claustrophobic recently. I want to move somewhere bigger.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Once I've made enough Mora, I'm going to buy a huge new house, as big as... Uh... At least as big as the Palace of Alcazarzaray!

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: That sounds really expensive...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: True. I'll never be able to afford it on a scribe's salary alone. I need to find another way...

dialogues.speaker: Isak
dialogues.text: Hi, Mr. Cyno. What are you thinking about?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: There's a chapter in "King of Invokations" where the spirit of someone who died long ago possesses a living man's body. To the outside world, it looks like he's developed a whole new personality.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I was just thinking how terrifying that would be for his friends. Imagine waking up one day to find that a friend of yours has suddenly become a different person...

dialogues.speaker: Isak
dialogues.text: Huh... So what got you thinking about that?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I don't know, but something feels off. Everything looks fine on the surface, but... Can human perception really be trusted?

dialogues.speaker: Khaldun
dialogues.text: Thank you, Sage Baladhuri. You really didn't have to stay with us to the end...

dialogues.speaker: Baladhuri
dialogues.text: Don't mention it. I'm your teacher, it's my job to look after my students.

dialogues.speaker: Khaldun
dialogues.text: Is Pania doing okay?

dialogues.speaker: Baladhuri
dialogues.text: I think so. She just left the city with her mother.

dialogues.speaker: Baladhuri
dialogues.text: This'll be her first trip away from home. She's handling it much better than I imagined. As her father, it's quite a relief... I just hope they have a smooth trip.

dialogues.speaker: Baladhuri
dialogues.text: Pack up your things. It's time we got going, too.

dialogues.speaker: Ruha
dialogues.text: Hey Mister, are you a robot?

dialogues.speaker: Nawid
dialogues.text: Shh... Look, he's pretending to be human! He definitely doesn't want anyone to find out he's a robot!

dialogues.speaker: Firnas
dialogues.text: I am a robot.

dialogues.speaker: Firnas
dialogues.text: I was designed to infiltrate the human world undetected. My mission is to find an opportunity... to destroy humanity.

dialogues.speaker: Ruha
dialogues.text: I knew it! It's just like in the picture books!

dialogues.speaker: Nawid
dialogues.text: What do we do? We're the only ones who know his secret, right? Surely he won't... silence us for good?

dialogues.speaker: Firnas
dialogues.text: You have discovered my secret. Now, I must take you as my prisoners. I will tickle your feet until you join the Robot Army.

dialogues.speaker: Ruha
dialogues.text: Waaaaaah!

dialogues.speaker: Nawid
dialogues.text: D—Don't be afraid! I'll protect you. Take this, robot!

dialogues.speaker: Firnas
dialogues.text: Ow, ow! Stop, stop... I was just kidding! I'm human, I'm human!

dialogues.speaker: Mu'izz
dialogues.text: *sigh* I can't believe I have to move so far away on such short notice...

dialogues.speaker: Kashif
dialogues.text: I made an automatic watering device so that my flowers won't wither and die while I'm away from home.

dialogues.speaker: Mu'izz
dialogues.text: Hey... do you think "renovation works" is the real reason they're moving us to Caravan Ribat?

dialogues.speaker: Kashif
dialogues.text: There's a rumor going around that Sumeru City's buildings aren't earthquake-resistant enough. Maybe that's it? All we know for sure is that the order came down from the Dendro Archon herself...

dialogues.speaker: Rima
dialogues.text: Hey, now's not a good time to visit Sumeru City. We're actually getting ready to move out ourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Tawfiq
dialogues.text: As if work and family aren't enough to deal with already! Now they're telling us to move to Caravan Ribat because of "renovations"? Hmph, I bet it's just some vanity project!

dialogues.speaker: Tawfiq
dialogues.text: I don't trust the Dendro Archon, nor any of the sages. Especially not that new Grand Sage — what's his name, Naphis? If you ask me, he's the worst of the bunch.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: (There's no one over there. I should go check out somewhere else instead.)

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: (It's like everyone's switched places...)

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: (I guess I'll keep looking around.)

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: (Everyone I know, everything I've ever known... Suddenly, it's all a jumbled mess...)

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: (The question is... Who's right, them or me? My head feels so heavy, I can't think straight...)
